description.description:
Canyoneering is an adventurous activity utilizing ropes, harnesses and descending equipment for rappels and other technical descents through canyons. Many of Arches National Park’s sandstone walls are cross-hatched with narrow passages making for excellent canyoneering. There are eight established canyoneering routes in the park outside of the Fiery Furnace.

This permit is not valid for the Fiery Furnace. If you are planning to canyoneer or hike in the Fiery Furnace you will need a specific permit.

description.need_to_know_email:
This is NOT your Permit!

To obtain your permit:

  • Log into your account

  • Click on My Reservations in the drop-down menu

  • Click Print Permit, then Yes. (Pop-up blocker must be disabled).  This will generate a PDF for you to print or download.

You must have a copy of your permit either printed or on a mobile device during your trip.

Planning to canyoneer in the Fiery Furnace? Your entire party must also obtain a Fiery Furnace Self-Guided Exploration permit. Reservations for Fiery Furnace permits are limited and are made available at 8 am MT 7 days in advance. They often sell out quickly.

Canyoneering Safety:

  • Canyoneering has inherent risks and you assume complete responsibility for your own safety.

  • You are responsible for knowing and abiding by all park rules and regulations as well as the information in the required video.

  • Honestly assess your own skill level and your limitations. You should not attempt routes that are not within your abilities.

  • Check the weather: Desert temperatures can soar above 100°F (37°C) in the summer, and plummet below freezing in winter. Late summer monsoons bring lightning, hail, rain, slippery rock surfaces, and flash floods.

  • Do your homework and know your route(s).

  • Inspect all fixed gear, especially knots in webbing: The harsh desert weather deteriorates webbing quickly. The National Park Service explicitly disclaims all responsibility for the safety of equipment, bolts, or anchor systems in the park. We do not maintain anchors.

  • Be prepared to self-rescue: Be prepared to know what to do in emergency situations – including injury treatment, evacuations, and changes in weather. If your trip leader gets hurt, can your group continue safely?

  • Report significant hazards and any injuries to a ranger

Contact Information: Backcountry Permit Office: canyres@nps.gov, 435-241-3110
description.need_to_know_order:
• A permit must be in your possession during the trip (printed or available on a mobile device). A permit is valid only for the dates, route, and number of people listed.

  • This permit is NOT valid for entry into the Fiery Furnace or for overnight use. Fiery Furnace Permits. 

  • You must watch the required video prior to your trip. Canyoneering safety is your responsibility. 

You are responsible for knowing and abiding by all park rules and regulations including seasonal route closures. 

  • Group limits are 6 persons for Lost and Found and MMI; 10 persons for all other routes. 

  • Travel on designated trails, roads, rock, and sandy washes only.  

  • Climbing, scrambling, walking upon, wrapping webbing or rope around, or rappelling off any named or unnamed arch with an opening greater than 3 feet is prohibited.  

  • All installation of new fixed gear requires a special-use permit .Fixed gear that is not associated with established routes will be removed. 

  • If an existing item or fixed anchor is judged unsafe, it may be replaced in kind without a permit. Software left in place must match rock surface in color.  

  • Use of deadman anchors is prohibited.  

  • Fixed ropes left in place for more than 24 hours are prohibited.  

  • Guided canyoneering services are prohibited. 

  • All garbage, including toilet paper, must be removed. 

  • Pack out solid human waste in a commercial, landfill safe waste bag. All toilet paper must be packed out. 

  • Pets are prohibited.  

  • The use of unmanned aircrafts is prohibited. 

  • Slacklining and BASE jumping are prohibited. 

  • All natural plants, objects, and cultural artifacts must be left where they are found. 

These are some of the park regulations. It is your responsibility to know and abide by all regulations .
description.need_to_know_permit:
A permit must be in your possession during the trip (printed or available on a mobile device). A permit is valid only for the dates, route, and number of people listed. Overnight travel or camping is not allowed.  

You are responsible for knowing and abiding by all park rules and regulations including seasonal route closures.  

Watch the required video prior to your trip. Canyoneering safety is your responsibility. Honestly assess you and your group’s skill level and know your limitations. You should not attempt routes that are not within your abilities or those within your group.  

  • This permit is NOT valid for entry into the Fiery Furnace. Fiery Furnace Permits. 
  • Group limits are 6 persons for Lost and Found and MMI; 10 persons for all other routes. 
  • Pets are prohibited.  
  • Travel on designated trails, roads, rock, and sandy washes only.  
  • Climbing, scrambling, walking upon, wrapping webbing or rope around, or rappelling off any named or unnamed arch with an opening greater than 3 feet is prohibited.  
  • All installation of new fixed gear requires a special-use permit . Fixed gear that is not associated with established routes will be removed. 
  • If an existing item or fixed anchor is judged unsafe, it may be replaced in kind without a permit. Software left in place must match rock surface in color.  
  • Use of deadman anchors is prohibited.  
  • Fixed ropes left in place for more than 24 hours are prohibited.  
  • Guided canyoneering services are prohibited. 
  • Pack out what you pack in. All garbage, including toilet paper, must be removed.
  • Human Waste: Always attempt to use a toilet beforehand and pack out solid waste in a commercial, landfill safe waste bag. All toilet paper must be packed out. 
  • The use of unmanned aircrafts is prohibited. 
  • Slacklining and BASE jumping are prohibited. 
  • All natural plants, objects, and cultural artifacts must be left where they are found. 
  • Overnight camping in Arches is only allowed in the Devils Garden Campground and by permit in a designated backcountry campsite. 

These are some of the park regulations. It is your responsibility to know and abide by all regulations . 

Park Entrance Pass

A park entrance pass (physical or digital) is required in addition to your canyoneering permit.
description.no_show_policy: Please cancel your reservation if you will not use it.
description.quota_details:
A permit is required for all canyoneering in the park. A permit is valid for one of the park’s established routes or for other non-established canyoneering routes. Other non-established canyoneering routes with fixed gear require approval and a special use permit .

A group may have up to three permits per day.   

To minimize the impact on park resources and visitor experiences the number of people per group is limited. Groups canyoneering in Lost and Found or MMI are limited to 6 persons. All other canyoneering groups are limited to 10 persons.
description.season_information:
A permit is required for all canyoneering trips.   

Established Canyoneering Routes:

Lost and Found, MMI, Bighorn, Tierdrop, Not Tierdrop, U-Turn, Dragonfly, and Elephant Butte

New Routes:

A special use permit is required for installation of new fixed gear. Contact CANYres@nps.gov for more information.

Group Size Limits:

  • Lost and Found and MMI have a group size limit of 6.

  • All other routes are limited to 10

Permit Availability:

  • Available online 8:00AM MT one day in advance up to 5:00PM MT the day of the trip. 

  • Self-issue permits are also available 24/7 on the Arches Visitor Center patio.

  • Permits must be readily available printed or on a mobile device during the trip.

Seasonal Closures

Some routes are closed seasonally, check the park website for closures .  

This permit is not for overnight camping.

description_map.need_to_know: Lost and Found/Undercover canyoneering route is in Lost Spring Canyon area of Arches National Park. Route access starts from outside the park boundary.
MMI canyoneering route is located in the Lost Spring Canyon area of Arches National Park. Route access starts from outside the park boundary.
Bighorn canyoneering route is along the Great Wall area in Arches National Park. There are multiple approaches for this route.
Dragonfly canyoneering route goes through a spur off Courthouse Wash in Arches National Park. Route access is from the main park road.
These canyoneering routes can form a loop across the Great Wall and Courthouse Wash areas. Route access varies.
Elephant Butte canyoneering route is located in The Windows area. Route access starts from the Garden of Eden parking area.
Tierdrop canyoneering route goes into Tierdrop Canyon. Route access starts from Park Avenue parking area.
Not Tierdrop canyoneering route goes into Not Tierdrop Canyon. Route access starts from Park Avenue parking area.
U-Turn canyoneering route goes into U-Turn Canyon. Route access starts from Park Avenue parking area.
These canyoneering routes go through U-Turn, Tierdrop, and Not Tierdrop canyons. Route access starts from Park Avenue parking area.
